items.q: The mucosal-injury causes of secondary IgA nephropathy include all of these EXCEPT:
items.exp: Mucosal injury: coeliac, Whipple, tropical sprue, Crohns, ulcerative colitis, HIV. (Book p772)

items.q: HIV sits in the mucosal-injury list, but its m/c associated glomerular lesion is:
items.exp: HIV (m/c collapsing FSGS) in the mucosal injury list; the liver-disease table pairs HIV with collapsing FSGS. (Book p772)

items.q: Cirrhosis appears as a secondary cause of IgA nephropathy because the damaged liver cannot clear immune complexes.
opts: True — the bracket reads 'liver cannot clear immune complex'
False — the bracket reads 'liver overproduces IgA'
False — cirrhosis is listed because portal hypertension damages glomeruli
True — and the identical reason is printed against hepatitis B
items.exp: Cirrhosis: (liver cannot clear immune complex). (Book p772)

items.q: The spondyloarthritis examples in adults are ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis and IBD-associated arthritis, where the book ranks:
In the innocent bystander mechanism, mucosal injury drives ↑↑ production of galactose-deficient pIgA, which is not cleared by liver; the antibodies formed against pIgA are:
items.exp: Anti glycan antibodies formed against pIgA → large immune complex. (Book p772)

items.q: In the innocent bystander mechanism, the large IgA complex cannot cross the sinusoids into the liver parenchyma and is finally deposited in the mesangium.
opts: True — hepatic vein, inferior vena cava, misdirected filtration at the glomerulus, mesangial deposit
False — Kupffer cells digest the complex before it reaches the inferior vena cava
False — the complex is deposited subepithelially rather than in the mesangium
True — and the page adds that the misdirected filtration is into Bowman's space
items.exp: Filtered at glomerulus (aqueous misdirected filtration) → deposited in mesangium. (Book p772)

items.q: Fill up: The glomerular filtration of the IgA immune complex is labelled ______ filtration.

Match each condition with its m/c associated glomerular disease — 1) HIV 2) Cirrhosis (alcoholic & non alcoholic) 3) Hepatitis C … A) Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis B) Collapsing FSGS C) IgA nephropathy
items.exp: HIV → collapsing FSGS; cirrhosis → IgA nephropathy; hepatitis C → MPGN. (Book p772)

items.q: Match each condition with the glomerular lesion printed against it in the liver-disease block — 1) Hepatitis B 2) Hepatitis C 3) Cirrhosis … A) Membranous nephropathy B) MPGN pattern C) IgA nephropathy D) Minimal change disease
Which pairing statement is TRUE per the m/c-associated-disease table?
opts: Cirrhosis, alcoholic and non-alcoholic, pairs with IgA nephropathy
HIV is paired with membranous nephropathy in the same table
Hepatitis C is the infection paired with collapsing FSGS
Hepatitis B is the virus listed beside an MPGN pattern
items.exp: Cirrhosis → IgA nephropathy; HIV → collapsing FSGS; HBV → MN; HCV → MPGN. (Book p772)
